analysis.title: FX Daily Snapshot: USD supported by improvement in AI investor sentiment
key_insights: DXY rose to a fresh year-to-date high of 104.53 on 23 Nov, lifted by a sharp rebound in US AI-related stocks and, to a lesser extent, higher US yields.

Nasdaq composite closed up about 6.5% on the day and 7.8% above Friday's low after the reported reinstatement of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia shares rose 31.3%, back to levels before his 12 Nov resignation.

President Trump reportedly dialled into the Nvidia board meeting to argue for Huang's return. MUFG says this signals willingness to intervene in company management and supports confidence given AI's weight in the US economy.

The 2-year Treasury yield rose about 4bps as markets grew more confident the Fed will keep tightening if the equity sell-off reverses. The Fed held in October partly because of tighter financial conditions for AI firms.
The Fed remains on course to hike again in December. Tighter financial conditions and gasoline prices down about 14.5% since late September cast doubt on multiple further hikes in 2027.

NY Fed's Williams said the Fed has 'work to do' on inflation and would not exclude hiking at consecutive meetings. He is watching markets 'very closely' and said a material, sustained change in AI optimism would affect his outlook.

EUR/USD fell to a year-to-date low of 1.0881, back inside the 1.0500-1.1000 range of 2023 to early 2025, when it averaged just below 1.0800. MUFG does not expect a break below that range absent a new euro area shock.
MUFG expects the euro to rebound gradually as the negative effects of the US-Iran conflict and euro area fiscal risks ease in the year ahead.
French-German bond spreads widened sharply in September and October and have stabilised at elevated levels, reflecting fiscal risk ahead of next year's presidential election.

Macron is considering a constitutional 'golden rule' for multi-year balanced budgets, particularly if markets stay volatile in January. It needs a three-fifths majority and Le Pen reportedly backs it. MUFG sees adoption as one potential positive euro catalyst.

market_movers.rationale: Shares surged 31.3% after the announcement that CEO Jensen Huang was reinstated 11 days after resigning, returning to pre-resignation levels.

sector_views.rationale: The Huang reinstatement could prove an important turning point for AI stocks into year end, but Williams flags a material, sustained fade in AI enthusiasm as a risk to the Fed outlook.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Fresh year-to-date high, supported by the AI equity rebound and higher US yields.
Year-to-date low, back in the 2023 to early 2025 range of 1.0500-1.1000.
Lower energy prices ease inflation pressure and cast doubt on multiple 2027 Fed hikes.
MUFG says the Fed remains on course to hike, with 2027 path less certain.

risk_factors: A material and sustained reversal in AI sector optimism would hit the US economy and the Fed outlook.
Further tightening in financial conditions could stop the Fed's hiking path.
A new negative shock for the euro area could break EUR/USD below 1.0500.
French fiscal risk and volatility in January markets.
Gasoline price increases could add to inflation pressure.
geopolitical: US-Iran conflict is cited as a negative influence on the euro.
French fiscal risk ahead of next year's presidential elections keeps French-German spreads wide.
Trump's involvement in the Nvidia board decision over a CEO tied to a suspected Chinese spy affair.
